Subject: Pathline Health — POC scope & SDK streaming/funcall asks

Hi Sanjay / Marta,

Thanks again for the call today — good discussion and appreciate the clarity around the triage use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I loop procurement in.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Claim triage latency: current search + rules pipeline is slow for high throughput (need <150ms 95th for embed-based retrieval)
- Inconsistent entity extraction across payers: need structured outputs (JSON model) to drive downstream routing
- Ranking signal quality: relevance of candidate documents needs reranking layer tuned to claims context

Goals for the POC (agreed):
1) End-to-end prototype: ingest 50k claim snippets -> retrieval -> embed + rerank -> structured extraction -> routing decision API
2) Validate latency and cost targets at small scale (100 qps burst, <150ms 95th on staging GPU instance)
3) Evaluate accuracy of structured extraction vs current rule-based baseline

Technical asks from Redwood side (what we’ll need):
- A sample of anonymized claim snippets (5k) and a short label set/expectations doc
- Confirmation on expected concurrency profile (avg qps and typical batch sizes)
- Decision on whether the reranker can be trained on Pathline-provided labels or we evaluate zero-shot

Proposed POC scope & timeline:
- Week 0: Exchange data sample + integration matrix (I attached a draft POC_scope_draft.pdf)
- Week 1–2: Redwood builds retrieval + embedding + streaming function-call prototype using streaming responses and function-calls for structured outputs
- Week 3: Reranking evaluation + latency tuning; initial cost estimates and pilot pricing

Open questions for you (please confirm by Mon):
- Will Procurement need an early MS or SOW? If yes, we can share an IDEA-level SOW this week.
- Any regulatory/compliance constraints on uploading even de-identified snippets (e.g., specific redaction rules)?

Next meeting: suggested Tuesday 4/21 09:30 PT to review the sample and confirm procurement path — does that work?

Attachments: POC_scope_draft.pdf (application/pdf), integration_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Kim — good write-up. Quick answers inline and a couple notes: 

- Sample data: we can provide a 5k de-identified CSV by EOD Monday. We’ll strip PHI per our standard — I’ll include the redaction checklist.
- Concurrency: typical traffic is 20–40 qps daytime, but we need to prove headroom to 100 qps burst.
- Reranker: initial plan is to start with zero-shot and then hand-label ~2k examples if results are promising.

Procurement loop: procurement@pathlinehealth.com (copied) wants an IDEA-level SOW and a very rough cost estimate for a 6-week pilot (hourly dev & infra + token estimate). They’ll take that into their internal approvals.

Regulatory: we’re fine with de-identified snippets but we must keep a log of who accessed the raw files — can we confirm retention/audit options?

Yes to Tue 4/21 09:30 PT. Also — Ben, Marcus: can you confirm whether streaming responses can carry both token stream and a trailing function-call payload in your prototype, or do you prefer a two-step (stream tokens then POST final function output)?

— Sanjay

Sanjay — thanks, copying short technical plan so you have it before Tue’s call.

TL;DR: We can prototype both approaches. Preferred is single-stream with trailing function-call to deliver structured JSON; fallback two-step if you need to separate token stream for UI.

Technical plan details:
- SDK: we’ll enable streaming responses with function-call support. Prototype will use: stream tokens -> final function_call(name="extract_claim_entities", arguments=JSON_SCHEMA)
- Structured outputs: we’ll ship a small JSON schema (entities, confidence, routing_decision) and include a lightweight validation layer in the SDK to catch malformed outputs
- Reranking: initial zero-shot reranker using our lightweight cross-encoder; we’ll expose an eval endpoint you can call with labeled pairs
- Latency: we’ll instrument 95th/99th with our tracing hooks and test on a dedicated small GPU pool (g4dn or equivalent) to measure 100 qps burst performance
- Audit/retention: Redwood Private supports audit logs; for hosted pilot we can enable 90-day retention + access logs for project scope — will confirm exact fields with Security team and share by Tue

Action items (owners):
- Pathline: deliver de-identified 5k sample + redaction checklist (Sanjay) — due Mon EOD
- Redwood: finalize POC SOW + rough pilot estimate for procurement (Kimberly) — deliver Mon EOD
- Redwood Eng: prototype streaming + function-call schema, deliver test harness + sample integration matrix (Ben/Marcus) — initial drop Wed

If any of the owners prefer different timings, call it out and we’ll reprioritize. Looking forward to the sync Tuesday.
